entry: Wrote config/datasets_manifest.tsv from the three research notes: 10x held-out mixtures, nuclei barnyard, xenografts, BD Rhapsody and Parse sets. Every link checked by a header or range request first.
Downloads started from a Studio tmux session, straight onto HPC3 through the transfer node (wget -c, resumable). Run id 20261116-2010_glymph-datasets.

STAR index job submitted for the combined human + mouse genome. Two species mixtures are public only as reads (BD Rhapsody GSE265962, Parse PRJEB67549), so their unfiltered matrices are rebuilt with STARsolo. BD barcode settings are the ones published by the RoCK/ROI authors; Parse barcodes come from the lists shipped with split-pipe 1.2.1. split-pipe itself is not installed in any environment on HPC3, and STARsolo keeps one aligner and one gene model for both mixtures.

ENA serves about 1 MB/s per file, and the four BD read files were holding up everything behind them. Restarted the driver so the Parse files download alongside (12 at once). The first Parse read links were wrong (my path rule; ENA uses 0 plus the last two digits) and returned 404; fixed in the manifest and restarted.

Added readers for BD Rhapsody tables (dense MolsPerCell csv, long Expression_Data st) and for GEO-style Parse folders; tested on synthetic files. Ingestion array submitted for the 39 libraries already downloaded: each becomes one standard .h5ad with unit, pool, vendor cell calls and labels where they exist.

Ingestion: 31 of 39 libraries converted in the first minute. GSE292578 (Parse, mouse fracture callus) turned out to hold counts for 15,190 barcodes only, although its matrix lists 1.42 million: the deposit is called cells, not an unfiltered matrix. It has no background barcodes and cannot be used; it stays in the table marked unusable.

Rank plots of the new platforms show the next gap. BD Rhapsody tables and Parse data have no droplet plateau: a knee, then a long tail. The plateau finder took the cell population of the BD spleen library for a plateau (threshold 11,194, 384 cells; the vendor calls 8,061), and the order-of-magnitude fallback put the Parse threshold at 12,000 to 50,000 counts.

Measured two candidate rules on all 43 + 12 libraries (job 59728185). (1) Homogeneity of the candidate plateau: the index of dispersion of gene counts across its barcodes is 1.01 to 1.30 for every true plateau (31 libraries) and 4.3 and 4.7 for the two that were really cells. Cutoff set at 2. (2) Knee as the lowest dip of the depth hazard: 8,087 barcodes above it for BD spleen (vendor 8,061), about 11,000 to 12,000 nuclei per Parse IGVF sublibrary, and within the authors' counts for the kidney nuclei (21,317 vs 20,046; 4,552 vs 4,566). The first dip from the top is not safe: on three human + mouse libraries it falls between the two cell lines, so the lowest dip above the floor is used.

Glymph prior step now has three modes: plateau (with the homogeneity check), knee, order of magnitude. It also reports a confident-cell depth (lowest gap above the threshold), used for calibration and for the output budget instead of the plateau's own "not plateau" threshold.

Calibration rewritten (exclusion.silent_budget). The 0.3.0 line through cluster summaries read the background 1.2 to 1.8 times too high on kidney because a few percent of doublets in a cluster look like background in a cluster sum. The new version fits every cell's count on its cluster's silent genes, kappa * ambient + s * depth, with a Poisson fit that drops cells and clusters carrying real expression. On simulated tissue with 5% doublets it recovers the per-cell background within 1 to 6% for three different mixes of ambient and swapped background. Tests pass on the Studio.

Development runs of this code submitted on HPC3 A30s for 22 libraries (5 kidney, 7 tier 1, 10 new ones including BD and Parse), with scoring chained after them. These are development runs on the tuning libraries, not benchmark results.

Read files: STAR index finished in 17 minutes. Mate order and sample identity checked on the files already complete (barcodes are in mate 1 for both platforms so far; the alignment job checks every pair and the archive md5). A Studio driver waits for the remaining read files, restarts stalled transfers, then submits the four STARsolo jobs and their ingestion.

Development round 1 (per-cell calibration, per-cluster silent genes): sensible on cell-line mixtures, but the depth-proportional term hit its cap on four of five kidney libraries and removal was 1.8 to 2.1 times the truth on kidney cells. Also the first gap finder skipped the real cell/background gap when a shallow dip between the human and mouse lines came first; fixed by merging dips of one valley and keeping the deepest.

Asked the kidney truth how background scales. In whole cells the genotype-based background per cell is flat with depth (about 0.8 to 0.9 empty-partition levels); in nuclei it rises with depth (nuc2: 344 + 0.17 per count). The metadata depth column is about half the raw depth, so an earlier reading of 0.4 levels was wrong. Proximal-tubule marker counts in other cell types are 1.0 to 1.4 times what truth x soup predicts, so marker leakage and genotype truth agree.

Silent genes are now those at the lowest peak of observed over expected background across the whole library (real expression only lifts a gene above background). Checked on finished outputs without retraining: kidney cells flat (1.05 and 0.99 levels, truth mean within 0.8 to 1.13), nuclei sloped, cell-line mixture unchanged.

Each cell gets its own ambient multiplier from its counts on its cluster's silent genes (empirical Bayes; the truth's mean background is 1.4 to 1.6 times its median, so one number over-removes for the typical cell). Development round 2: per-cell error and rank correlation beat the published CellBender 0.2.0 values on four of five kidney libraries (rep1 0.067 / 0.49 vs 0.084 / 0.44; rep2 0.081 / 0.51 vs 0.085 / 0.43; rep3 0.047 / 0.52 vs 0.052 / 0.37; nuc3 0.117 / 0.15 vs 0.168 / 0.10); nuc2 worse (0.157 / 0.19 vs 0.113 / 0.32). These are development runs against published numbers, not the benchmark.

Third term added for nuclei: ambient-profile background that grows with depth. Round 3 calibration, no labels used: kidney nuc2 constant 0.60 + depth 0.44 (truth 0.55 and 0.47), whole cells depth term 0.

Parse bone marrow (2 million barcodes, about 300 million entries) ran out of memory on a 24 GB card in the output step. The per-gene budget is now computed over blocks of genes; identical result (tested).

config/datasets.tsv now says how each library was used in development: 12 tuned on (seven cell-line mixtures, five kidney), 10 looked at (run during development and results seen), 32 held out (never run with Glymph before the benchmark), 1 unusable. Held-out libraries include seven 10x mixtures, five xenografts, both BD Rhapsody and both Parse species mixtures and seven Parse tissue sublibraries.

Followed the background amount down the pipeline on the kidney truth cells: calibration matched the truth (0.8 to 1.17 of the truth mean) but the model's posterior multiplier settled 18 to 32% below its calibrated value in every library. With per-cell multipliers set, the posterior is now pinned to them (round 4): removal on nuclei rose from 73% to 99% and 89% of the truth.

Output rule: the per-gene budget takes counts mostly from shallow cells (kidney: shallow cells lost 1.0 to 1.2 times their background, deep cells 0.5 to 0.7). A rule that also keeps each cell's expected background total (thinning.gene_cell_budget) cut per-cell error on nuclei from 0.144 to 0.127 and raised rank correlation on the tuning mixtures from 0.61 to 0.73, for 0.3 points less cross-species removal (round 5). Adopted.

Vivek, mid-run: Glymph needs something that clearly distinguishes it from CellBender, or reviewers will read it as a tweak. Answered that the identity to build on is measuring the background from internal negative controls (silent genes) where CellBender infers it from a likelihood and priors. Saved as project guidance.

Exclusion constraint added: after calibration the decoder may not express a cluster's silent genes, so counts on them can only be background and the likelihood itself fixes each cell's load (rounds 8 and 9). Tuning mixtures: 95.0% of cross-species counts removed (CellBender in the first run: 94.3%), per-cell error 0.0074 (0.0167); kidney marker leakage removed from other cell types rose from 85% to 90% in nuclei. Adopted. A loose prior with its level matched after training (rounds 6, 7, 9) was no better than pinning and costs a third training phase; not adopted.
Dashboard updated: libraries table (55 libraries with tier, platform, truth, status, development use, cell counts), the dataset run, its jobs and this log.

False-positive budget on the seven tuning mixtures, current code: 0 gives 92.8% removed and no native loss; 0.2% gives 94.2% and no native loss; 0.5% gives 95.0% and 0.11% native loss. CellBender 0.3.2 at its default of 1%: 94.3% and 0.024%. Per-cell error 0.0074 to 0.0087 against 0.0167 at every setting. The benchmark will run both tools' curves: CellBender writes budgets of 0, 0.5% and 1% from one training run (20_cellbender_array.sbatch, CB_FPRS).

Instability found in the confirmation round: on kidney nuclei the calibration sometimes settles on a second answer with the swapped term at its cap and about a fifth too much background (three earlier runs gave constant 0.60 + depth 0.44, two later ones 0.23 + 0.74 + cap). Cause: the fitted swapped fraction feeds into which genes count as silent. Freezing that feedback made nuclei stable across three seeds (38 to 40% removed, truth 39.4%) but removed the swapped term from a cell-line mixture that needs it (round 11). Round 12 keeps the feedback and lets a smaller group define the lowest ridge.

Last read file arrived (ENA served about 1 MB/s per file; two transfers were restarted by the driver). STARsolo jobs 59729712 to 59729715 submitted for the two BD Rhapsody and two Parse species mixtures, ingestion 59729717 after them. The alignment job checks every file against the archive md5 first; all four passed.

Calibration rule settled after rounds 11 and 12: keep the feedback, let a small group define the lowest ridge, lean 3% against the swapped term, cap it at 5%. Kidney nuclei across three seeds: constant 0.56 to 0.59 + depth 0.47 to 0.54 every time (truth 0.55 and 0.47). On the seven tuning mixtures at a budget of 0.5%: 94.1% removed with 0.07% native loss, per-cell error 0.0076 (CellBender 0.3.2 in the first run: 94.3%, 0.024%, 0.0167). Default false-positive budget set to 0.4%, where same-species removal equals its expected value on those mixtures. All four test files pass. Glymph 0.3.0 frozen.

The BD Rhapsody alignment had matched no barcode at all: the dataset uses the 96-label barcode set, not the 384-label one. Checked against the reads and the authors' label file, switched lists, added a check that at least 30% of reads carry a valid barcode, and reran (92 and 94% valid; 9,899 and 7,983 cells; every author-labelled cell found). Parse sublibraries aligned on the first try (63% valid barcodes, 81% uniquely mapped; the barcode mate differed between runs and was detected per pair).
All 54 usable libraries are in the standard format. Dataset phase done; the benchmark is run 20261116-2209_glymph-alltier-bench.
